title: How to make a slip knot in thread
subtitle: When a slip knot is useful and how to tie one that releases cleanly.
excerpt: A slip knot in embroidery thread is used to secure a skein bundle during storage and as a temporary starting knot before snipping. It is the one knot that releases with a single pull.
sourceNotes:
Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), Internet Archive. Knots and thread preparation for hand embroidery.
Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776. Thread handling and preparation.

glossaryTerms.definition: A knot that slides along the thread and releases with a pull on the free end. Used to bundle skeins during storage and as a temporary starting knot removed after the thread is anchored by stitches.

content.text: in embroidery has two uses: bundling a cut skein to stop it tangling, and as a temporary starting knot you can remove by pulling the free end once the thread is anchored. It is the one knot that belongs on the back of a piece, because it comes out before the work is finished.
How to tie a slip knot
Hold the thread between your left thumb and forefinger, with about 10 cm of free tail.
Make a loop by crossing the working thread over the tail end.
Reach through the loop and pull a bight (a small folded section) of the working thread back through the loop.
Pull the tail end to tighten the knot around the bight. The knot slides along the working thread.
To release, pull the free end of the thread that was drawn through the loop. The knot drops away immediately.

attrs.heading: What goes wrong
attrs.intro: Common slip knot problems in needlework use.

items.symptom: The knot doesn't release when the free end is pulled
items.cause: A plain overhand knot was tied instead of a slip knot, or the wrong end was pulled.
items.fix: Pull the shorter free end, not the longer working end. If the knot still won't release, use scissors and re-tie. Check you are pulling a bight, not a full loop.

items.symptom: The knot tightens and jams on the thread
items.cause: The thread was pulled too tight when tying.
items.fix: Tie the slip knot loosely so the bight can still move. A tight slip knot is no longer a slip knot.

content.text: The slip knot bundles thread skeins neatly in storage and makes the away-knot starting method easier to remove. The
